note: Keys in `outputs` are FORMAT KINDS, not outputs[] labels. This stack's outputs[] labels are the caller-chosen group_name of each requested output group (plus the fixed `probe` and `usage`), so labels cannot be enumerated here. Each group entry's `desc` is joined by the group's format kind, read from the run's reconciled output_groups — never from the file extension, because a jpeg/png group's output object is frame_manifest.json. `probe` and `usage` join directly by label.
stability: Every entry in `outputs` is stable API: format kinds, basename patterns, and the field names/nesting shown in each example. Removing or renaming any of them is a breaking change and requires a TOOL_VERSION bump plus a changelog note here. Files NOT listed here (segment_video/ .ts and segment_audio/ .flac chunk intermediates — deleted after a successful merge unless KEEP_SEGMENT_CHUNKS is set — and anything else under the prefix) are internal and may change or vanish without notice. `description` is one line by design — it is joined verbatim into each get_job_status outputs[] entry as `desc`.

mp4.description: Transcoded H.264 (openH264) MP4 proxy — use for playback, review, vision pipelines; audio is one AAC 96 kbps 48 kHz stereo track regardless of source layout

contents.video: H.264 (openH264), request width x height (default 960x540), deinterlaced when the source is interlaced, +faststart
contents.audio: AAC 96 kbps, 48 kHz, 2-channel — re-encoded from the stereo-downmixed FLAC intermediate; absent for video-only sources

mp4.notes: {name} defaults to the group_name; the object lives at {prefix}/{group_name}/{name}.mp4. Not master-referenced: the audio track is derived from the shared 2-channel FLAC intermediate (channel selection and downmix already applied), so it does not preserve the source channel layout.

wav.description: Extracted PCM WAV audio (pcm_s16le, default mono 48 kHz) — use for ASR or waveform work; derived from a stereo-downmixed intermediate, not the master channel layout

contents.audio: pcm_s16le; audio_channels (default 1) and sampling_rate (default 48000) from the group parameters, applied at merge

wav.notes: {name} defaults to the group_name. The shared .flac intermediate is always 2-channel stereo; the group's final channel count is applied at merge, so a mono WAV is a downmix of that stereo intermediate.

m4a.description: Extracted AAC M4A audio (default stereo 48 kHz 96 kbps) — use for compact audio delivery; derived from a stereo-downmixed intermediate, not the master channel layout

contents.audio: AAC; audio_channels (default 2), sampling_rate (default 48000), audio_bitrate (default 96 kbps) from the group parameters, applied at merge; +faststart

m4a.notes: {name} defaults to the group_name. Derived from the same shared 2-channel .flac intermediate as every other audio group.

jpeg.description: Frame-capture manifest for a jpeg group — the group's output object; use to enumerate the captured frame_NNNNNNN.jpg files under the group prefix
jpeg.notes: The manifest IS the output object output_keys points at for a jpeg group; the actual frames live under `prefix` and `keys` lists them (basenames relative to `prefix`, frame_{N:07d}.jpg with N the source frame number, stepping by ceil(fps x frame_interval_sec)). `dimension` is the frame [width, height] in pixels.

png.description: Frame-capture manifest for a png group — the group's output object; use to enumerate the captured frame_NNNNNNN.png files under the group prefix
png.notes: Identical shape to the jpeg manifest; only the key extension differs (.png). The manifest IS the output object for the group — the frames live under `prefix` and `keys` lists them.

metadata.description: Resolved technical metadata (duration + its source rung, is_all_intra, stream facts) plus the detail-filtered ffprobe dict — use for codec/resolution/duration/timecode questions without transcoding
metadata.notes: {name} defaults to metadata.json. `mxf` is present ONLY for MXF sources — absence means not-MXF; presence means every field is a real mxf2raw measurement. `mxf.frame_count` and `mxf.duration_sec` are omitted when the MXF header records no duration (count=-1, valid on e.g. Sony eVTR D10); `mxf.start_timecode` is omitted when absent. `video` is present only when the source has a video stream. `duration_sec`+`duration_source` and `is_all_intra` are resolved facts, not ffprobe passthroughs; `is_all_intra` may be null for ambiguous codecs. `probe_info` is the ffprobe dict filtered by the group's `detail` level (`full` adds per-stream disposition/tags); its interior shape is ffmpeg's, not this stack's contract.

probe.description: Probe-state envelope around the verbatim ffprobe result (probe_info) — use for raw stream/format facts; prefer a metadata group for resolved facts like is_all_intra
probe.notes: `probe_info` is the verbatim, unfiltered `ffprobe -show_format -show_streams -show_chapters -show_programs` output — its interior shape is ffmpeg's and is NOT a stable contract shape; only the envelope fields shown are. `iterators` is the internal chunk plan ([] on a metadata-only run) — do not integrate against it.

usage.description: Per-state durations and estimated cost — use for reporting what this run cost
usage.notes: Costs are us-east-1 pricing estimates, not billing data. `retried` counts attempts that ended in TaskFailed (routine — chunk-transcode retries are normal); `incomplete` is true only when an attempt has no terminal event at all. Both are absent from the final `Usage tracking` entry, which estimates itself before its own terminal event exists. This stack's usage shape differs from its siblings' usage_tracking.json — do not assume cross-stack parity.

ad_mix.description: Audio-description mix: the programme audio ducked (sidechain) under the narration takes placed by the AD workflow's render_manifest.json, loudness-normalized (I=-24, TP=-2) — stereo PCM WAV, proxy-grade bed (stereo-downmixed intermediate, not the master layout)

contents.audio: pcm_s16le; audio_channels (default 2) and sampling_rate (default 48000) from the group parameters; duration pinned to the programme bed

edit_manifest.description: Quick-edit evidence manifest — requested vs actual per cut (ms + frames), the derived record timeline, crops (ratios and pixels), normalizations, transitions, overlays, measured loudness, source ETags

capture_manifest.description: Frame-capture manifest for a capture_frames run — maps each marker index to its still's key with requested vs actual ms and the source frame number (replaces frame_manifest.json for this mode; the group label still joins the jpeg/png entry)
